abstract: In view of high coefficient of friction and poor wear resistance of titanium alloy, laser processing method is used to form grooves on the surface of titanium alloy, and the grooves surface of titanium alloy is coated with titanium dioxide films to improve the wear resistance of titanium alloy. Friction tests were carried out on three surfaces of titanium alloy respectively in this paper: smooth surface, groove surface, groove surface coated with titanium dioxide films. A comparative analysis of wear depth and morphology different test conditions were conducted accordingly. The experimental results show that titanium alloy groove surface coated with films has the lowest coefficient of friction, produces the shallowest scratch depth and the least wear, Titanium alloy grooves surface coated with films, however, is very slightly different from titanium alloy grooves surface. In addition, titanium alloy grooves surface coated with films has the least increase of oxygen after wear.

articleTitle: Plate-like Metal Oxide Nanostructure for Detection of Small Metabolites by Mass Spectrometry
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Novel plate-like metal oxide nanostructure was demonstrated for analysis of small metabolites by laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI MS). We prepared the nanoplates using hydrothermal method. Owing to the unique nanostructure and physicochemical properties, our method displayed high sensitivity and high accuracy towards the analysis of standard molecules and metabolites of serum samples. The nanomaterials also indicated great salt tolerance and protein endurance in complex biosamples in LDI MS. This work provided an innovative matrix for metabolic analysis and clinical diagnose in LDI MS.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of Copper Powder Smoke on Laser Transmission Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: according to Mie theory, the extinction, absorption, and scattering coefficient of a single copper particle was simulated by Mie-plot, the radius of a single copper particle was 3 μm. Using the Lambert-Beer law, the transmission of the laser at 532 nm, 650 nm and 980 nm through copper powder smoke is calculated. It was taken single scattering of particles in account, when the laser transmission was simulated. It can be seen from the simulation results that the transmission of three kinds of typical lasers have a trend of decrease with the increase of the particle number concentration. The curves of transmission of laser operating at 532 nm and 980 nm are very close. The transmission of laser operating at 650 nm is less than the other slightly. The experiments of laser transmission through copper powder smoke were performed. The experimental results show good agreement with simulation analysis results in the lower particle number concentration. The simulation value is higher than the experimental value obtained with the increase of particle number concentration, that the multi-scattering occurs in the process of laser transmission is the main reasons.

articleTitle: Development of Wide-area Tip-scanning High-speed Atomic Force Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Recently a tip-scanning type high-speed atomic force microscopy (HS-AFM), which is combined with total internal reflection fluorescence microscope (TIRFM), has been developed. Using this system, the topographic and fluorescence images of biological samples in action have been simultaneously visualized. However, the maximum scanning range of the combined system was limited to ~20 μm and ~3 μm in X- and Y-directions respectively. This limitation makes it impossible to visualize the dynamics of much larger samples, including bacteria or mammalian cells. Here, we improved a laser-tracking system and expand the tracking range in X- and Y-directions to ~50 μm and ~32 μm, respectively by increasing an angular variation of a mirror-tilter unit changing the arrangement and the adhesive area between piezoactuators and base plate of the unit. The Shift of the X-direction of the scanner with large displacement of the Z-scanner is eliminated by modifying an input triangular signal to the mirror-tilter unit. We also developed a scanner, which could cover in a wider imaging area, for the expanded mirror-tilter unit in the tip-scanning HS-AFM system. The capability of this expanded system is demonstrated by measuring the laser-spot displacement, large-area imaging of a square grating sample and eukaryotic cells.

articleTitle: Molecule Concentration Dependence of DNA Translocation Configuration through Solid-state Nanopores
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this paper, we studied the effects of DNA concentration and diameter of solid-state nanopores on DNA translocation configuration. Experimental results show that co-translocation of DNA molecules events is prone to occur at a high DNA concentration. Because the number of DNA molecules present in the capture region of the nanopore would increase with increasing DNA concentration, and it causes DNA molecules to be captured simultaneously into the nanopore by an external electrical field. It is found that decreasing bias voltage barely eliminates the phenomenon of co-translocation. However, capture region is conspicuously reducing along with the nanopore size. For nanopore with the diameter of 24 nm, most of DNA molecules pass through the pore in a linear translocation state.

articleTitle: Growth of Nerve Cells Induced by Diverse Nanopillar Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The nanotopographies can induce the growth of nerve cells and the growth of their synapses. Studying the anisotropic structures for the guidance of neuronal synapses is beneficial to the in vitro repair of neurons and the development of regenerative medicine. Thus, studying how diverse nanopillar arrays affect the growth of nerve cells is essential. This paper employed the technology of laser interference lithography (LIL) to fabricate different nanopillar arrays with the same and different size gaps between the X and Y directions, and observe how the structures induce the growth of nerve cells and their synapses.

articleTitle: Research of High-precision Virtual Instrument Test Platform for Linear Displacement Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: High-precision virtual instrument acquisition platform of linear displacement sensor is an instrument that has standard interface. It helps to insert different displacement sensor into the platform. It is framed into high precision, integrated, modular and testing various types of displacement sensor system. The platform utilizes the virtual instrument technology which is assembled by high speed computer, data collection system and software. The platform can provide standard interface for different types of linear displacement sensor, identify the sensor type, collect data and process data automatically. Therefore, it becomes a part of displacement sensor calibration system. Intelligent acquisition platform of linear displacement sensor is a part of displacement measuring system, but it is also a part of displacement sensor calibration system. So, the influence of platform accuracy must be ignored. From the theoretical analysis and experimental verification, we can see that the uncertainty component of platform is 0.033%, the uncertainty is less than 1/3 of secondary instrument.

articleTitle: Melting of Metall Nano Particles for Nanoassembling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The size effect on the melting temperature of metal nanowires and nanoparticles was studied under action of resistive heating and laser irradiation in the vacuum chamber of scanning ion microscope and TEM. The 100 nm thick In nanowires were produced by FIB milling, the 20 - 200 nm In and Au nanoparticles were produced by laser ablation. The partial melting of indium particles at t ~ 55 °C was demonstrated, which is at least 100 degrees less than melting temperature of a bulk In sample. As a result of heating by the laser, a partial melting of the submicron In nanowire was also observed below bulky sample melting point. The results of the study of size effect on melting of metal nanosamples can be applied to development of the new technology of low-temperature nanosoldering of nanoelectronic parts, fibers, lamellae etc.

articleTitle: The Effect of Micro-column Structure on Surface Wettability of Aluminum Alloy
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The superhydrophobicity of solid surfaces is primarily dependent on low surface energy and surface microstructure. In order to prepare a low-wetting surface, a micro-column array was constructed on the surface of aluminum by micro-milling and grinding, and the influence of the square-column structure on the surface wettability of the material was analyzed. Milling will cause burrs on the surface of the square column. Under the joint action of the square columns and the burrs on the surface, the contact angle of the material surface increased from 50.3° to 98.4°. After grinding, the burr on the surface of the square column disappears, but the irregular secondary groove structure is formed at the top of the groove, which further improves the contact angle of the surface of the test piece (127.8°). On the whole, the construction of the micro-column structure enhances the hydrophobic properties of the aluminum alloy surface. The micro-grinding square column structure can further realize the transition of the wettability of the aluminum alloy surface from hydrophilic to hydrophobic, and the contact state of the water droplet on the surface thereof is in the transition state of Wenzel and Cassie.

articleTitle: Novel Perovskite-Based Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Organic-inorganic hybrid perovskite attracts huge interests due to its outstanding properties. Here, three kinds of perovskite devices have been developed, including resistive switching memory, position-dependent photodetector and graphene-perovskite hybrid phototransistor. The resistive switching memory shows extremely low operating current and synaptic characteristics. The position-dependent photodetector could realize millimeter-scale detectivity. The phototransistor reaches the peak photoresponsivity of 600 A/W and shows great stability in ambient environment in 75 days. These results demonstrated that both 3D single crystals and 2D flakes of perovskites can be used for many fields, especially for electronic and opto- electronic device applications.

articleTitle: The Study on Surface Integrity on Laser-assisted Turning of SiCp/2024Al
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: An experimental study was conducted on laserassisted turning (LAT) of SiCp/2024Al in order to investigate the effects of input variables of LAT and conventional turning (CT) on machining performance of SiCp/2024Al. An experimental study was conducted on LAT of SiCp/2024Al in order to investigate the effects of input variables of LAT and CT on machining performance of SiCp/2024Al. The process benefits of laser processing variables were analyzed by comparing the surface roughness, surface microstructure and residual stress. The variables in LAT are as follows: the cutting speed is 30 to 60 m / min, the feed rate is 0.01 to 0.1 mm/rev, and the laser power is between 0 W and 50 W. The experimental results show that under the same cutting parameters, the LAT outperforms the CT method by reducing the surface roughness value by up to 81.73%. Unlike in CT, LAT produces more residual compressive stress. Micro-structure analysis shows that there are no microcracks on the surface of the workpiece machined by LAT.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of a Novel Wheel-Type Piezoelectric Nanopositioning Motor with Centimeter-scale Stroke
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In order to solve the conflict between high precision and large stroke in the micro/nano operation field, this paper presents the development of a flexure-based wheel-type motor (WTM) driven by piezoelectric(PZT) actuators, which can generate end-effector motion in the range of over 30cm and with subnanometer resolution. In nano-positioning, the short stroke of the PZT actuator limits the process of development and application. The conventional lever displacement amplification mechanism cannot fully fix the requirements of practical applications. The structure designed in this paper, wheel drive structure (WDS), which has relative small size. The devise of WDS converses intermittent stroke into the wheels rotation, which is finally shown as continuous linear output. Especially, the WTM is composed of asymmetric hinges, which produces an arc motion through parasitic displacement. With the character of the structure, there is no limit to the stroke of the output theoretically. After mechanical optimization design, the matrix-based compliance modeling (MCM) method is adopted for static modeling, dynamic modeling and transient modeling of the device. Finally, the reason by finite element analysis (FEA) method is satisfied to inspect the performance of WIM.

articleTitle: Design of Vision Assistant System for an Atomic Force Microscopy Based on Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper designs a vision assistant system for an atomic force microscopy based on object detection. The system includes a visual interface, a focus assessment subsystem, a function that evaluates the uniformity of the object distribution and an object detection subsystem. A visual interface can provide researchers a convenient way to obtain the area of interest. Afterwards, the sharpest image in the region of interest can be obtained by the automatic focus of the focus assessment subsystem. Furthermore, the object distribution uniformity function is proposed to find an optimal region with uniform object distribution. Based on the above modules, the object detection algorithm is proposed to detect and locate the objects, which provides reliable visual assistant for the imaging and manipulation of an atomic force microscopy. Experimental results are exhibited to illustrate the good performance and the satisfactory robustness of the system.

publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Summary form only given.
